title: Frozen Apache Jira response caches for the architectural-refactoring study (v1)
description:
2,491 Apache Jira REST API v2 responses, pulled 2026-07-19, covering 323 architectural tickets in the Apache Hadoop ecosystem (HADOOP, HDFS, YARN, MAPREDUCE, HDDS, OZONE, SUBMARINE) plus their status changelogs, issue properties, assignee records and a matched control set.

Why this is deposited rather than scripted. Jira is live. Issues are edited, reopened and occasionally deleted, so a re-fetch returns a different state and no rebuild script can reproduce this snapshot. Every statistical result in results_dossier.md is computed from these files. The archive ships with a per-file SHA-256 manifest and no rebuild script, deliberately: a rebuild script would imply a reproducibility that does not exist.

Contents. .jira_cache 323 files (raw issues, 31.12 MB); .jira_changelog 323 (status transition histories); .jira_control 400 (matched ordinary-ticket control arm); .jira_props 722; .jira_assignee 723. Uncompressed 32.11 MB.

Integrity. Archive SHA-256 fcb705b664c248d0c4d32f69b854e10fd8b11c907a19c40333322e06d31b9a95. Per-file digests in MANIFEST-v1.json.

Personal data. Records carry Jira author and assignee display names, which are public on issues.apache.org. scripts/pseudonymize.py in the code repository removes them if a pseudonymised copy is wanted.

Analysis code and results are at https://github.com/khannoussi-malek/refactoring-review-friction, which also carries the pre-registered predictions, the six failed hypotheses with named causes, the retracted Cox result, and a provenance row for every number.
notes: Source: Apache Software Foundation public Jira, https://issues.apache.org/jira. API pulls 2026-07-19T00:27:37Z to 2026-07-19T20:04:44Z; archive created 2026-07-25T04:49:20Z.
